Explosion lab — the colour round

"is space explosions only blue, whats the thought process there?" — you, on this board. It was a fair question with no good answer, so here is the answer as a comparison: every one of the nineteen candidates now appears twice, side by side — COLD in the plasma register it was authored in, and RED in the threat-red one. Thirty-eight options, all playable. Press ▶ Play both and the pair fires on the same instant; click one canvas to play just that option.

Red is legal, and it is legal for the reason you gave. Threat red is not a player's colour — it is a STATE colour meaning danger: enemy fire is shotEnemy1/2/3 ("unmistakably threat red"), damage fills are red, alarm rings are red. A ship coming apart is a danger event, so red on an explosion is not a new meaning smuggled into a reserved hue, it is the meaning that hue already carries. Signal yellow is a different matter and it does not move. Yellow is ore, ore is what you scan a field for all match long, and an explosion that went ore-yellow at its brightest would teach a player that yellow sometimes means something else. Nothing on this page burns yellow, at any brightness — the ore glints in the asteroid family are ore, and they are the only yellow here.

The comparison is colour and nothing else, by construction. A red twin is not a second candidate: it is the same emit function, off the same seed, writing the same positions, velocities, lifetimes, radii and alphas — run into a pool that maps the colour column on the way past. There is exactly one copy of the motion, so the motion cannot drift between the two panels. The whole treatment is two colours: plasma → threat red and plasmaHot → shotEnemy3, which are the same point on the same value ramp in the other register (both are their base mixed 45% toward WHITE). Red climbs toward white, never toward orange — that is the one way to get this wrong, because a red that brightens through orange lands on ore's colour at the exact moment it is biggest and brightest.

What the map cannot reach. It is keyed on the colour of LIGHT, so it warms flares, sparks, embers and shockwave rings and it is structurally incapable of touching rock chips, hull shards, smoke, ash, dust, the repair channel or the ore payout. Debris is not on fire. Each red panel prints how many of that candidate's particles it actually repainted, and IDENTICAL is a real and frequent answer in the asteroid family.

In every family the first candidate is today's effect, labelled TODAY. ▶ Play family fires every panel in the family at the same instant, which is the only honest way to judge six deaths against each other.

Everything here is the game's own particle system, drawn by the game's own renderer. Real ParticlePool, real PARTICLE kinds in their real colours, the real update loop, and the real VfxLayer — the client's only particle draw path — on a real WebGL renderer. Today's three rows are literally explosion(), stationDeath() and asteroidBurst(). Nothing in src/ changed: this page is the decision, the port is the follow-up.

Replay is exact. Each candidate is emitted from a seeded mulberry32 and stepped at a fixed 1/60, so two viewings of one candidate are identical and a comparison is a comparison — on a 60 Hz monitor and on a 144 Hz one alike. Nothing autoplays.

Scale is true. Each frame is world space — the ship, the facility and the rock are the shipped sprites at their shipped radii, on the game's own Floor #070910, and nothing is scaled up to photograph better. That is why the station frames look emptier: a station's shockwave is 288 units wide and the frame has to be big enough to hold it.

The stills are still here, under each live panel and smaller: 0.05s · 0.15s · 0.35s · 0.6s · 1s · 1.5s. A single instant is the way to judge a single instant, and they are plain SVG, so they show even if the live half cannot run.

Answer with one id per family — "B-R, J-C, N-C" is a complete answer. Every option carries a fixed id, printed on its own panel, so a verdict can name exactly one of the two colours as well as one of the shapes. Two answers are also fine: if the shape is settled and the colour is not, say so.

Live playback is unavailable in this browser — the filmstrips below are the whole page for now.

Ships

A ship is cheap and respawns free, so this one is allowed to be quick and bright. The variable is the balance of flare, sparks, shards and smoke.

Every ship candidate has real light in it — a flare, a shockwave, embers, sparks — so every red twin here is a genuinely different frame. This is the family where the question was asked and it is the family with the most to say back.

Frame: 300 world units across. Vanguard hull at its collision radius, 16 world units (SHIP_RADIUS). The body is drawn at 35% as a ruler — it is there for scale, not because it is still standing.

All 6 at the same instant — the only honest way to judge 6 deaths against each other. Loop is off until you ask for it: an effect that is fine once and irritating on the tenth loop has told you something.

Stations

GDD §4.7 makes this the most serious moment in the game — the audio drops out for three seconds and nobody jokes — and the shipped effect says in its own comment that it is "deliberately not a firework". Four of the five candidates keep that stance and vary weight and duration instead. L is the one that does not, and it is here so the departure is something you decline on purpose.

A station death is mostly mass: shards, smoke and a shockwave. So the red twins of G, H and I move a handful of embers and the wave, and J and K — the two candidates whose whole character is that NOTHING burns — have only their wave to repaint. If red reads as heat, a red wave on an implosion may be exactly the heat those two were written to refuse; that is worth looking at rather than assuming.

Asteroids

Your direction, verbatim: "more dust based perhaps?". Today is chips and a shockwave — a small bomb. Every candidate here leads with dust: slow, low-alpha cloud that hangs and drifts, chips as an accent, and the ore glints kept, because the payout is why anyone shot the rock. Six candidates, not five — this is the family with the most room in it.

YOUR DUST DIRECTION IS ABOUT MATERIAL, NOT HEAT, AND THE MAP AGREES WITH IT. A rock is not on fire: there is no fuel and no oxygen, and the thing coming off it is powdered stone. The treatment repaints LIGHT — plasma into threat red — and five of these seven candidates contain no light at all, so their red twin comes back identical, particle for particle. Only M and Q have a shockwave ring, and that ring is the only thing red can reach here. That is the argument, and it is made by the map rather than by this paragraph: if you want warmth in a rock burst it has to come from a new particle, not from a recolour, and the honest place for it would be the hit that broke the rock rather than the dust that followed.

Frame: 200 world units across. Rock at stage 2 — one hit from bursting — at radius 24 world units. Rocks run 22–46 units, but 24 is the radius EVERY burst is drawn at today however big the rock was: the observer packs magnitude as radius/24 clamped to 1, and the field unpacks it as magnitude×24. The body is drawn at 20% as a ruler — it is there for scale, not because it is still standing.

All 7 at the same instant — the only honest way to judge 7 deaths against each other. Loop is off until you ask for it: an effect that is fine once and irritating on the tenth loop has told you something.

How to read a strip. Left to right: 0.05s, 0.15s, 0.35s, 0.6s, 1s, 1.5s. The particle count on the right of each header is the busiest frame, against a pool capacity of 1600 shared with everything else on screen — so it is also the cost.

What is deliberately not here. No candidate invents a motion, a blend mode or a particle shape: all nineteen are built from the eleven shipped kinds, which is what makes a pick a tuning rather than a rewrite. The red treatment adds no seventh hue either — it reuses threatRed and shotEnemy3, both already in the palette and both already meaning danger. The ore glints in the asteroid family are signal yellow, which is legal and load-bearing — ore is one of the two things that colour is allowed to mean, and it is the one thing on this page red is never allowed to become. The four looks the treatment can reach at all are spark, ember, flare, ring — the four made of light. The other seven are matter, and they come through untouched.

The third option nobody has asked for yet. The map warms every light in an effect, shockwave ring included. If what you want is red embers over a cold wave — heat from the fire, cold from the pressure — that is a real third treatment and it is one line to add. Say so and it will be here.

Nothing has been ported. Not one byte of src/ changed for this round; the red looks live in the lab. A pick is what moves them into the game.

The station family's stance. G, H, I, J and K all keep the shipped one: no sparkle added, the weight and duration of the collapse varied instead. L is a labelled departure — it is what a firework at station scale looks like, so that declining it is a decision rather than an omission.
